title: Chapter 1 Quiz 7
description: A mixed review of Chapter 1. Say how sure you are before you check.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which of these is **not** required of an algorithm?
options: It must give at least one result
It must always need input data
It must end after finite steps
questions.explanation: An algorithm may or may not need input. It must be finite, definite and give at least one output. Watch out: the question asks for what is not required.

questions.question: A program that runs but gives wrong results has a syntax error.
questions.explanation: Wrong results from a program that runs point to a semantic (design) error. Watch out: syntax errors stop the program from running at all.

questions.question: Put these stages in order.
questions.explanation: Analysis, algorithm, coding, compiling, running. Watch out: the algorithm is written before the coding, not after.

questions.question: Match each symbol to its function.
questions.explanation: The four main flowchart symbols. Watch out: the rectangle is for processing, not for input and output.

questions.question: Place the shapes on the flowchart that tests whether a number is positive.
questions.explanation: Input and output are parallelograms, and the question x > 0 ? is a diamond. Watch out: the display is an output, so it is also a parallelogram.

questions.question: The course writes Avg ← g1 * c1 + g2 * c2 + g3 * c3 / (c1 + c2 + c3). With grades 8, 12, 10 and coefficients 3, 2, 5, what does a computer calculate?
questions.explanation: The division comes first: 10 × 5 = 50, 50 / 10 = 5. Then 24 + 24 + 5 = 53. Watch out: the correct weighted average is (24 + 24 + 50) / 10 = 9.8, and it needs brackets around the sum.

questions.question: A {{1}} error is reported by the {{2}}, and no executable program is produced.
questions.explanation: Syntax errors break the rules of the language, so the compiler cannot translate the program. Watch out: a semantic error is not reported by the compiler.

questions.question: Which stages are done automatically by the machine?
questions.explanation: Analysis and coding are human work. Compilation and running are automatic. Watch out: coding is writing the source, which a human does.

questions.question: This algorithm should display the perimeter of a square. One line has an error.
questions.code:
Declare side, perimeter As Integer
Read(side)
perimeter ← 2 * side
Display(perimeter)
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides, so perimeter = 4 × side. Watch out: 2 × side is half of the perimeter, a number that looks plausible.

questions.question: Complete the structure of the algorithm in the correct order of its parts.
questions.code:
{{1}} Average
Declare g1, g2, g3, Avg As Real
Start
    Read(g1, g2, g3)
    Avg ← (g1 + g2 + g3) / 3
    Display(Avg)
{{2}}
questions.explanation: The name is preceded by ALGORITHM, and the body that begins with Start ends with Stop. Watch out: Start is already used to open the body, so it cannot close it.

questions.assertion: The compiler produces an executable program for any source program.
questions.reason: Syntax errors prevent translation into machine language.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false: with a syntax error no executable program is produced. The reason is true. Watch out: the reason explains why the assertion is false.

questions.question: Which of these tasks is done by the **programmer** and not by the machine?
options: Reporting the syntax errors found in the source
Compiling the source program into machine language
Translating the algorithm into a programming language
Executing the executable program on a computer
questions.explanation: Translation of the algorithm into code is a human intellectual operation. Watch out: the compiler reports errors, but writing the code is not its job.
